hero_subtitle: Morocco’s garden city in the Middle Atlas — cool air, cedar forests, lakes and ski slopes above 1,600 m.

overview.title: An alpine town that feels unlike the rest of Morocco
overview.p1: Ifrane sits high in the Middle Atlas at about 1,650 m, planned in the 1920s–30s as a garden city with pitched roofs, flower beds and wide avenues. Locals call it Little Switzerland — not for the Alps, but for the cool summers, winter snow and a pace that feels European next to Fez or Meknes.
overview.p2: You come for clean air, walks around Dayet Aoua, the cedar forest with Barbary macaques, Michlifen’s high plateau, and easy day links to Azrou. It is a base for nature more than monuments: lakes, forests and ski slopes when the season allows.
overview.p3: Two days cover the town, a lake and the cedars. A third day opens Michlifen, a second lake or a slow national-park trail. Pack a jacket even in summer — evenings drop fast.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Town and lion first, lakes and cedars second, heights or park third.

day1.title: Town centre & Source Vittel
day1.morning: Start at the stone lion and walk the clean avenues. Source Vittel park for a gentle introduction to the garden-city layout.
day1.afternoon: Al Akhawayn campus exterior if open to visitors. Coffee in the centre. Short valley walk toward Tizguit if energy remains.
day1.evening: Early dinner — Ifrane nights cool quickly. Rest for a full nature day tomorrow.

day2.title: Dayet Aoua & cedar forest
day2.morning: Drive or taxi to Dayet Aoua for lakeside walks and birdwatching. Soft light is best before midday.
day2.afternoon: Cedar forest for macaques and tall Atlas cedars. Keep distance from monkeys; no feeding.
day2.evening: Return to Ifrane. Simple grill or hotel dinner.

day3.title: Michlifen or second lake
day3.morning: Michlifen for high views and, in season, ski or snow play. Or Dayet Hachlaf for a quieter water loop.
day3.afternoon: Ifrane National Park trail if you want more forest. Or continue toward Azrou and the cedar market.
day3.evening: Pack for Fez, Meknes or the Atlas route south.

detailed_itinerary.title: Hour-by-hour ideas
detailed_itinerary.subtitle: Flexible blocks you can swap around weather and opening times.
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start at the stone lion and walk the clean garden-city avenues; Source Vittel park shows the town plan.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: See the campus edge if accessible, then coffee in the centre. Short valley walk toward Tizguit if energy remains.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Dine early — Ifrane nights cool fast even in July.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Drive or taxi to Dayet Aoua for shore walks and birds. Morning light is best.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Continue to the cedar stands for Barbary macaques. Do not feed the monkeys; close bags.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Simple grill or hotel dinner after the forest day.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Michlifen for high views (ski in season) or the quieter Dayet Hachlaf loop.
detailed_itinerary.day3_a: Afternoon — National park trail or Azrou
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: A short park path, or continue toward Azrou market if you leave the plateau.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Bags for Fez, Meknes or deeper Atlas routes.

1.title: Pack layers
1.desc: Even in July, evenings are cool. A light fleece saves the dinner walk.

2.title: Respect the macaques
2.desc: Do not feed or chase monkeys in the cedar forest. Keep bags closed; they are skilled opportunists.

3.title: Car or organised day helps
3.desc: Lakes and Michlifen are spread out. A driver for one day unlocks more than taxis alone.

transport.title: Getting around without wasting time
transport.desc: The town centre is walkable. Lakes, Michlifen and the cedar forest need a driver or organised half-day — taxis alone eat time and budget.

bargain.title: Shopping and expectations
bargain.desc: Ifrane is not a souk city. Buy simple supplies in the centre; cedar crafts are easier in Azrou market if you continue that way.

water.title: Layers, altitude and timing
water.desc: Even in summer, evenings are cool at 1,650 m. Pack a jacket. Start lake and forest walks in the morning; avoid feeding macaques.

q1.question: How many days in Ifrane?
q1.answer: Two days cover town, one lake and the cedars. A third day fits Michlifen or a second lake without rushing.

q2.question: Is Ifrane worth visiting?
q2.answer: Yes if you want cool air, forests and a break from medina intensity — especially between Fez and the deeper Atlas.

q3.question: Do I need a car?
q3.answer: Helpful. Town is walkable; lakes and Michlifen are easier with a driver or organised half-day.

q4.question: Best season?
q4.answer: May–June and September–October for mild walks. December–February for snow if you want winter sports.

q5.question: Safe for families?
q5.answer: Yes — open parks, calm centre, clear nature stops. Supervise children near lakes and monkeys.
